variables.title: Variables & Constants
variables.notes: Java is statically typed. The 'var' keyword infers type only for local variables. 'final' makes a variable a constant.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Java distinguishes between primitives (lowercase, fast) and Object wrappers (Capitalized, required for Generics).

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: Remember to use '.equals()' for object comparison, as '==' compares object memory references, not values.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Java 14 introduced modern switch expressions that return values and use lambda-like arrows, preventing fall-through.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: The enhanced for-each loop is generally preferred for arrays and collections unless the index is explicitly needed.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: While loops work standardly. Do-while loops are useful when the logic must execute before the condition check.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Java methods must be part of a class or interface. Static methods can be called without instantiating the class.

arrays.title: Arrays / Lists
arrays.notes: Native arrays have fixed sizes. Collections like ArrayList are dynamic and heavily favored in modern Java.

maps.title: Maps / Dictionaries
maps.notes: HashMap is the standard implementation. 'Map.of' creates unmodifiable maps easily.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Java has 'Checked' exceptions (must be caught or declared) and 'Unchecked' RuntimeExceptions.

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.notes: Java uses C-style // single-line and /* */ multi-line comments.

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Java provides explicitly sized integer and floating-point primitives with binary and hex support.

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.notes: Java uses bool / boolean types with true and false literals and logical operators (&&, ||, !).

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Conversion
type_casting.notes: Java supports explicit type casting using cast operators or constructor functions.

strings.title: Strings & Characters
strings.notes: Java distinguishes between single-character literals and string sequences or pointer slices.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Java supports string interpolation or printf-style formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching & Switch
pattern_matching.notes: Java evaluates branching conditions through switch statements, match expressions, or when constructs.

range.title: Ranges & Slicing
range.notes: Java represents ranges with range operators (.., ..<) or standard indexed iteration boundaries.

iterators.title: Iterators & Sequences
iterators.notes: Java implements iteration through Iterator interfaces, generators, or range-for loops.

oop_classes.title: Classes & OOP
oop_classes.notes: Java models object orientation through classes with constructors/encapsulation or structs with associated methods.

lists.title: Dynamic Arrays & Lists
lists.notes: Java manages growable dynamic collections using vectors, ArrayLists, or dynamically reallocated heap buffers.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Java represents heterogeneous records through tuples, structured bindings, or lightweight record structs.

sets.title: Sets & Unique Collections
sets.notes: Java provides unique collection hashing structures with O(1) average lookup and insertion time.

modules_import.title: Modules, Packages & Imports
modules_import.notes: Java structures namespaces and external libraries via include directives, package declarations, or module imports.
